title: A Query Engine for Scientific Data Exploration using Theory, Simulation, and Artificial Intelligence Models
problem: Modern scientific workflows couple simulations, heterogeneous data, and AI models but lack unified query interfaces. Existing systems force scientists to fragment workflows, losing efficiency and interactivity.
motivation: Scientific discovery increasingly relies on integrating diverse computational resources (databases, simulators, AI models). Current tools lack expressive query language and execution engine to compose these resources efficiently with low latency.
method: IDS (Intelligent Data Search): A unified query engine combining in-memory datastore (feature store, vector store, knowledge graph), model repository (UDFs, pre-trained AI), and distributed multi-tier cache. Integrates Cray Graph Engine with keyword, set-theoretic, and linear-algebraic operators.
key_novelty: Unified query engine spanning data retrieval and model inference; integration of simulations (AutoDock Vina), AI models (AlphaFold), and analytics (Smith-Waterman) in single query; distributed multi-tier caching for performance.
contributions: IDS framework unifying data query and model inference
Unified query language spanning keywords, sets, and linear algebra
Model repository for pre-trained AI and simulations
Demonstration on life-sciences workflow (AlphaFold + AutoDock Vina + Smith-Waterman)
Millions of similarity searches and thousands of model inferences in tens of seconds

metrics.query_latency: Tens of seconds for millions of similarity searches + thousands of inferences

limitations: Requires integrated system deployment; performance depends on cache locality; specialized for scientific workloads.
